questions.question: Which helping verb is used with 'I' and 'We' in the traditional Future Indefinite rule?
questions.rationale: Traditionally, 'I' and 'We' take 'shall', while 'You', 'They', 'He', 'She', 'It', and names take 'will'.

questions.question: "When you ___ me, I will help you." Choose the correct verb.
questions.rationale: In an if/when clause referring to the future, use Present Indefinite ('help'), not will/shall — the main clause takes Future Indefinite.

questions.question: What is the structure of Future Continuous Tense?
questions.rationale: Future Continuous Tense follows: Subject + will/shall + be + V1 + ing, e.g., 'They will not be working without money.'

questions.question: For a Yes/No interrogative future sentence, what is the correct pattern?
options: Helping Verb + Subject + Main Verb + Object?
Subject + Helping Verb + Main Verb + Object?
questions.rationale: Closed (Yes/No) interrogative sentences begin with the Helping Verb, followed by Subject + (not) + Main Verb + Object, e.g., 'Is he reading books?'
